# AGENTS.md

**This file is the source of truth for agent instructions.** Add agent guidance here and nowhere else; do not add a `CLAUDE.md`.

## What this is

An OpenCode V2 plugin that runs agent workflows as a state machine. A workflow is a tree of steps and blocks (`each`, `loop`) in a file; the engine alone decides the next step. User-facing behavior is documented in `README.md`. This file covers what an agent needs to change the code safely.

## Commands

| Goal | Command |
|---|---|
| Install | `pnpm install`, then `bun run hooks` once for the git hooks |
| Everything CI runs | `bun run check` |
| Lint and format | `bun run lint`, `bun run format` |
| Types | `bun run typecheck` |
| Tests | `bun test` |
| Unused code and dependencies | `bun run knip` |

## Layout

| Path | Role |
|---|---|
| `src/workflow/steps.ts` | The five step builders, the `each` and `loop` blocks, their options, workflow validation over the tree |
| `src/engine/state.ts` | Run state (position: a path in the tree plus one frame per enclosing block), events, state version |
| `src/engine/tree.ts` | Pure navigation of the tree: what a path designates, document order, the outline kept in the state |
| `src/engine/reducer.ts` | `reduce(workflow, state, event)`: pure, no I/O. Every transition rule lives here |
| `src/engine/executor.ts` | Runs the current step through the ports, applies the event, persists |
| `src/ports.ts` | `AgentRunner`, `UserGate`, `Checks`, `Git`, `RunStore` |
| `src/adapters/` | OpenCode (sessions, verdict tool, hooks), shell, git, disk |
| `src/locks.ts` | What a step session may run and edit: pure, tested in `test/locks.test.ts` |
| `src/shared.ts` | State that outlives a reload of the plugin (tracked sessions, runs being driven) |
| `src/builtins.ts` | Built-in `code` steps |
| `src/commands.ts` | One command per workflow, plus `/workflow`. Tested in `test/commands.test.ts` |
| `src/loader.ts` | Loads workflow folders (`<name>/<name>.ts`) and their agent files (`<name>/agents/*.md`) |
| `src/skill-proof.ts` | Reads, from the message OpenCode stored for a prompt, that each requested skill arrived: pure, tested in `test/skill-proof.test.ts` |
| `src/index.ts` | Server plugin entry. Registers the agents of workflow folders |
| `src/kit.ts` | Types of a workflow file (`opencode-steps/kit`). Imports nothing from OpenCode nor from Node, so a workflow file type-checks with this package alone |
| `src/tui.tsx`, `src/tui/view.ts` | Interface part: status line segment and sidebar block. `view.ts` is pure and tested, and also prints the outline of `/workflow status` |
| `src/published.ts` | Where the server part leaves the interface part its settings (the interface part gets no plugin options) |
| `src/tui/update.ts` | When a newer version of the plugin is installed: pure, tested in `test/update.test.ts`. Only the host's check and install are used |
| `skills/` | Skills the plugin registers. `src/skills.ts` loads them |
| `docs/` | User documentation |

The engine never imports OpenCode. Only `src/adapters/opencode.ts`, `src/index.ts` and `src/tui.tsx` do.

A change to a step, an option or a command updates `README.md`, `docs/reference.md` and `skills/writing-workflows/SKILL.md` in the same commit.

## Rules that must hold

- The reducer stays pure. A new transition rule is a reducer change with a scenario in `test/reducer.test.ts`.
- An absent result is `step_blocked`, never `step_succeeded` nor `step_failed`.
- No step names another step; control flow is nesting. The run reads the tree top to bottom, and only `each` (next item) and `loop` (repair, restart) move it elsewhere. Never add an option that jumps by name.
- Every loop has a cap: a `loop` without an integer `max` of at least 1 is rejected at validation.
- An option is offered only on the kinds of step it acts on, and validation refuses it elsewhere.
- `state.json` carries `version`. A change to the shape of the state raises `STATE_VERSION`; an older file is reported, never driven nor crashed on.
- Locks are denials. Never add an `allow` rule or an `ask`.
- Skills are attached by code to the first prompt of a session and proven from the message OpenCode stored. Never leave loading a skill to the agent.
- Errors are `Result` values. Ports do not throw.
- A workflow agent is created by `editor.update` on an unknown id: the agent editor has no `add`. OpenCode applies the agents of the configuration after those of plugins, so a name conflict is only visible from `context.agent.list()` once everything is registered, never inside the transform.
- A refused prompt rejects with a tagged error whose `message` is empty (`{ _tag: "Session.SkillNotFoundError", skill }`): read its fields, not its message.
- Sessions of a step are created without `parentID`: with one, OpenCode wakes the main session's model each time a child ends.
- User approval goes through `/workflow` commands. OpenCode 2.3.0 gives plugins no way to show a form.

## Tests

Scenarios, given / when / then, on the reducer and on the engine with ports mocked by `bun:test`. Test behavior a user would notice; no test for wiring or mapping.

## OpenCode versions

`@opencode/plugin` is pinned to an exact version. Before raising it, replay a real run in an isolated instance (`XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_DATA_HOME`, `XDG_STATE_HOME`, `XDG_CACHE_HOME` pointed at a scratch directory, `opencode serve` on a private port, clients with `--server`): the command, the step sessions and their denials, `session.wait`, the verdict tool and the tool hooks all depend on APIs that may change.

## Commits and releases

Conventional Commits. release-please owns versions, tags and `CHANGELOG.md`: never edit them by hand. Branch from `develop`, open the PR against `develop`.

# Writing workflows

A workflow is one folder in the workflows directory (`~/.config/opencode/workflows/` unless the plugin option `workflowsDir` says otherwise): `<name>/<name>.ts`, with its own agents in `<name>/agents/<agent>.md` and any prompt file it reads. It is a tree of steps read top to bottom. Code picks the next step from each step's result, so the order never depends on a model. The indentation is the control flow: no step names another step.

Write the folder, run `/workflow reload`, then `/workflow status`: it lists the workflows that loaded and the problems of those that did not.

## Before writing

Ask the user, one question at a time, until you can fill this table. Do not guess a row.

| Question | Becomes |
|---|---|
| What starts the run, in one sentence? | the ticket passed to `/<name> <ticket>` |
| Which parts need the user in the conversation? | `talk` steps |
| Which parts are done by one agent? Which agent? | `agent` steps |
| What proves the work is right, as commands? | `check` steps |
| Who reviews, and from which angles? | `parallel` step |
| Which steps must be redone together when a verification fails, and how many times? | a `loop({ max }, [...])` around them |
| Who repairs a failure, if not the producer? | `repair` of that `loop` |
| Is there a list to work through one item at a time? Is each item one commit? | `each(key, { commit }, [...])` |
| Where must the user say yes? | `approve` |
| What is mechanical (worktree, push, cleanup)? | `code` steps |

Then list the agents the workflow names and check each exists (`agents/*.md` in the OpenCode config, or a built-in such as `build`). A missing agent blocks the run at that step. An agent only this workflow uses goes in the workflow's `agents/` folder.

## The file

`~/.config/opencode/workflows/ship/ship.ts`:

```ts
import type { Kit } from "opencode-steps/kit"

export default ({ workflow, talk, agent, parallel, check, loop }: Kit) =>
  workflow("ship", [
    talk("scope", { writes: "spec.md", approve: "scope" }),
    loop({ max: 2 }, [
      agent("build", { agent: "build", prompt: "Implement the spec. Tests first." }),
      check("checks", { commands: ["npm test"] }),
      parallel("review", { agents: ["reviewer"] }),
    ]),
  ])
```

- The default export is a function of the kit. Import nothing at runtime from `opencode-steps`: the `import type` line is erased and only gives types.
- The workflow name is the slash command and the folder name: lowercase letters, digits and dashes. `workflow` is reserved.
- Step names are unique in the whole tree, repair steps included.

## Steps

| Step | Use it for | Ends when |
|---|---|---|
| `talk(name, { skills, writes, prompt })` | A discussion with the user in the main session. It may write only `writes`, a file of the run directory. | The main session submits its verdict. |
| `agent(name, { agent, model, skills, prompt, writes, output, deny, timeoutMs })` | Work by one agent in its own session. `model` (`"provider/model"` or `"provider/model#variant"`) replaces the model of the agent's definition. | It submits `done` or `blocked`. |
| `parallel(name, { agents, model, skills, prompt, deny, timeoutMs })` | Read-only reviewers, at the same time. An entry is an agent name or `{ agent, model, name, prompt, when, skills }`; an entry's `model` wins over the step's, its `skills` add to the step's. | Each submits `approved`, `needs_fixes` with findings, or `blocked`. |
| `check(name, { commands, timeoutMs })` | Shell commands run by code. Defaults to the `checks` list of the run data. | Every command exits 0, or one fails. |
| `code(name, { run })` | A function without a model. Built-ins by name: `isolate`, `setup`, `push`, `cleanup`. | The function returns. |

`approve: "label"` works on every step. `deny` only on `agent` and `parallel`, `timeoutMs` only on `agent`, `parallel` and `check`: elsewhere they would do nothing, so the workflow is refused.

| Block | Use it for |
|---|---|
| `each(key, { commit }, [steps])` | Run `steps` once per item of `data[key]`. Every step of the block gets the item. With `commit: "field"`, the work tree is committed after each item with that field as subject. `{ commit }` can be left out. |
| `loop({ max, repair }, [steps])` | Restart `steps` from the first one when one of them fails, `max` times at most. `repair` is one `agent` step run before each restart. |

## Rules the engine applies

Know them, because they decide how you nest the steps.

1. A step that succeeds goes to the next step of its block. After the last step of a block, `each` starts its next item and `loop` goes on after the block.
2. Only `check` and `parallel` fail. A failure restarts the closest enclosing `loop`, after its `repair` if it has one, with the failure as `feedback`. After `max` restarts, one more failure blocks the run. A failure outside any `loop` blocks the run.
3. Without `repair`, the failure is given to the restarted steps; it is kept until a `talk`, `agent` or `parallel` step succeeds, and dropped when the run leaves the loop. A restart runs everything again: an `each` inside a `loop` starts again at its first item, so put the `loop` inside the `each` to retry one item.
4. `approve` makes the run wait: `/workflow approve`, `/workflow revise <remarks>` (same step again with the remarks) or `/workflow back` (closest `talk` step written before).
5. `each` reads its list once, when the block is entered: empty or missing blocks the run. Nested `each` blocks give every step `items`, the item of each block, outermost first. After each item, `commit` commits the work tree, then the next item starts. A `loop` inside starts every item with no restart used.
6. An agent that returns nothing (crash, limit, timeout, no verdict after one reminder) blocks the run. It is never a success and never an ordinary failure.
7. Agents cannot `git commit`, `git push` or use `gh`. Use `each` with `commit`, `code("push")` or a `code` step of your own.
8. `onFail`, `max` or `then` on a step and `each` on a step are refused with the block to write. Any option a step or block does not have is refused too (`writes` on a `check`, `max` on an `each`).

## Patterns

**Check loop.** The producer and its verifier in one `loop`.

```ts
loop({ max: 2 }, [
  agent("write", { agent: "build" }),
  check("checks", { commands: ["npm test"] }),
]),
```

**Review with a repair step.** `fix` only runs on a failure, then the block restarts from `checks`.

```ts
loop({ max: 3, repair: agent("fix", { agent: "build" }) }, [
  check("checks", { commands: ["npm test"] }),
  parallel("review", { agents: ["reviewer"] }),
]),
```

**Plan, then one commit per task.** The planner submits structured data; the `each` block iterates it.

```ts
const Plan = z.object({
  checks: z.array(z.string()).min(1),
  tasks: z.array(z.object({ title: z.string(), commit: z.string(), brief: z.string() })).min(1),
})

code("isolate"),
agent("plan", { agent: "planner", output: Plan, approve: "plan" }),
each("tasks", { commit: "commit" }, [
  loop({ max: 2 }, [agent("implement", { agent: "build" }), check("checks")]),
]),
code("push"),
code("cleanup"),
```

**Reviewer only when needed.** `when` names a key of the run data.

```ts
parallel("review", { agents: ["reviewer", { agent: "sql-reviewer", when: "sql" }] })
```

## Prompts

`prompt` is a string or a function of `{ ticket, runDir, worktree, data, item, feedback }`. `item` is the item of the closest enclosing `each`. The engine already adds the ticket, the current item, the feedback to address, the paths, and the rules about the verdict tool. Write only what is specific to the step: the goal, what done looks like, and what to put in the verdict.

Workflow files run on Bun, so Bun's APIs are available (`import.meta.dir`, `Bun.file`, `Bun.$`). Keep long prompts in files next to the workflow and read them when the file loads:

```ts
const brief = async (name: string): Promise<string> => Bun.file(`${import.meta.dir}/prompts/${name}.md`).text()
const plan = await brief("plan")
```

`/workflow reload` picks up a changed prompt file: the workflow file is loaded again when any file of its folder changed. For editor types, the workflows directory needs `@types/bun` and `"types": ["bun"]`.

Only `<name>/<name>.ts` (or `.js`, `.mjs`) is loaded as the workflow, so other files of the folder are safe for prompts. A workflow file at the top of the workflows directory is not loaded: move `x.ts` to `x/x.ts`.

## Skills

`skills: ["name"]` on a step, on a `parallel` entry or in an agent file. The plugin attaches them to the session's first prompt and checks they arrived with their content: the agent has nothing to load. A skill that is not installed blocks the run with `skill "name" was not loaded`. Order, without duplicates: the agent file's, the step's, the entry's. The older `skill: "name"` is refused at validation: write `skills: ["name"]`.

## Agents of a workflow

`<workflow>/agents/<agent>.md`, the file name being the agent's name:

```md
---
description: Writes the implementation plan of a ticket
model: claude-agent/opus
skills: [writing-plans]
---
You write the plan of the ticket you are given, task by task.
```

Fields: `description` (required), `model`, `mode` (`subagent` by default, `primary`, `all`), `hidden`, `skills`, `permissions` (`{ action, resource, effect }`). Any other key is reported. The body is the system prompt. Give it a name no other agent has. When a built-in agent or an agent of your configuration has the same name, yours is the one that runs (OpenCode applies a configuration agent on top of the workflow's), the skills of the workflow's file are not attached, and `/workflow status` reports it.

## Run data

What an agent submits in `data` (validated by `output`) and what a `code` step returns are merged into the run data. Name the keys once and reuse them: `tasks` for `each("tasks", ...)`, `checks` for `check`, `setup` for `code("setup")`, `branch` and `title` for `code("push")`.

## Checklist before handing over

- Every `check` and `parallel` that may fail is inside a `loop`, unless a failure must stop the run.
- Every `loop` has a `max`, and holds the steps to redo: the producer and its verifiers.
- A `repair` is one `agent` step; its name is unique like any step.
- An `each` whose items must be committed has `commit`, naming a field the plan fills.
- Every agent named exists, and every skill named is installed.
- Every `check` command exists in the repositories the workflow will run on.
- A reviewer never needs to edit: reviewers are read-only and must leave the work tree as they found it.
- `/workflow reload` then `/workflow status` shows the workflow and no problem for its folder or its agent files.
- Try it once on a throwaway repository before a real ticket, and read `events.ndjson` in the run directory: it shows every transition, every refused tool call and the skills proven loaded in each session.

## When a run blocks

The main session says why and where the run directory is. Run `/workflow status` for the tree with the current step and the counters, then read `events.ndjson` and `reports/`. Fix the cause by hand, then `/workflow resume`. Common causes: a missing agent or skill, a check command that does not exist, a loop that reached its `max`, a failure outside any `loop`, an empty `each` list, an agent that tried to commit. A run started by an older version of the plugin cannot be resumed: `/workflow abort`, then start it again.

# opencode-steps

Deterministic agent workflows for [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) V2. You write the steps in a small file, as a tree read top to bottom. Code decides what runs next, from each step's result. No model chooses the order, so no step gets skipped.

Work in progress: built and tested against OpenCode 2.3.0. The plugin API it uses is young and may change without notice.

## Why

A skill or an orchestrator agent describes a process in prose, and the model decides how closely to follow it. Here the process is a state machine:

- a step hands over only when its exit condition is true, checked by code;
- a `loop` block restarts its steps until they pass, up to a cap;
- an agent that returns nothing (crash, limit, timeout, no verdict) blocks the run. It never counts as a success or as a normal failure;
- agents cannot commit, push or ask for permissions.

## Install

Add the plugin to your OpenCode config (`~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`):

```jsonc
{
  "plugins": ["opencode-steps@git+https://github.com/axelhamil/opencode-steps.git"]
}
```

Then put each workflow in its own folder of `~/.config/opencode/workflows/`: `<name>/<name>.ts`, with the agents it needs in `<name>/agents/`. Each workflow becomes a slash command named after it.

The plugin also brings a skill, `writing-workflows`, so an agent can write the workflow with you, and shows the current run in the status line and the sidebar of the terminal UI.

Documentation: [getting started](docs/getting-started.md), [writing workflows](docs/writing-workflows.md), [reference](docs/reference.md), [how it works](docs/how-it-works.md).

## A workflow

```ts
// ~/.config/opencode/workflows/review-loop/review-loop.ts
import type { Kit } from "opencode-steps/kit"

export default ({ workflow, agent, check, parallel, loop }: Kit) =>
  workflow("review-loop", [
    loop({ max: 2 }, [
      agent("write", {
        agent: "build",
        prompt: "Implement the ticket in the work directory, with its tests.",
      }),
      check("checks", { commands: ["npm test"] }),
      parallel("review", {
        agents: [
          { agent: "build", name: "correctness", prompt: "Review the uncommitted changes against the ticket." },
          { agent: "build", name: "simplicity", prompt: "Review the uncommitted changes for code the ticket does not need." },
        ],
      }),
    ]),
  ])
```

Read it top to bottom: `write`, then `checks`, then `review`. When `checks` or `review` fails, the `loop` restarts from `write` with the failure as feedback, twice at most; a third failure blocks the run.

Run it from any session with `/review-loop <ticket>`. That session becomes the main session of the run: progress, blocks and requests for your approval arrive there, and you pilot the run from it.

The file's default export is a function that receives the kit (`workflow`, the five step builders, the `each` and `loop` blocks, and `z` from Zod), so it needs no install of its own. The file runs on Bun, the runtime OpenCode runs plugins on, so Bun's APIs (`Bun.file`, `Bun.$`, `import.meta.dir`) are available. The `import type` line is optional and only gives you types and inline documentation; with `@types/bun` and `"types": ["bun"]` your editor also knows Bun's APIs. To have them in your editor, see [Types in your editor](docs/writing-workflows.md#types-in-your-editor).

## The five steps

| Step | What it does | How it ends |
|---|---|---|
| `talk(name, options)` | The main session discusses with you. It may only write the file named by `writes`, inside the run directory. | The main session submits its verdict when you both agree. |
| `agent(name, options)` | One agent in its own session. | The agent submits `done` or `blocked`, with `data` if the step has an `output` schema. |
| `parallel(name, options)` | Several agents at the same time, read-only. | Each submits `approved`, `needs_fixes` (with findings) or `blocked`. All approved: the run moves on. Any findings: the step fails. |
| `check(name, options)` | Shell commands run by code, in order. | Exit codes. A failing command fails the step, with its output as the failure. |
| `code(name, options)` | A function, no model. Built-ins: `isolate`, `setup`, `push`, `cleanup`. | The function's result. |

## The two blocks

| Block | What it does |
|---|---|
| `each(key, { commit }, steps)` | Runs `steps` once per item of the list `data[key]`, in order. Every step of the block receives the item. With `commit: "field"`, the work tree is committed after each item with the item's `field` as subject. An empty or missing list blocks the run. `{ commit }` can be left out. |
| `loop({ max, repair }, steps)` | Runs `steps`. When one of them fails, `repair` (one `agent` step) runs with the failure, then `steps` restart from the first one; without `repair`, they restart with the failure as feedback. After `max` restarts, the next failure blocks the run. `max` is required. A restart runs everything again: an `each` inside starts again at its first item. |

Only `check` and `parallel` steps fail. A failure restarts the closest enclosing `loop`; outside any `loop`, it blocks the run. Blocks nest freely. No step names another step: the indentation is the control flow.

### Options

| Option | On | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `approve: "label"` | every step | After the step succeeds, the run waits for you with `waiting for you to approve the <label>`: `/workflow approve`, `/workflow revise <remarks>` (same step again, with your remarks) or `/workflow back` (closest `talk` step written before, or the same step when there is none). |
| `deny: [{ action, resource }]` | `agent`, `parallel` | Extra permission rules denied to the step's agents. |
| `timeoutMs` | `agent`, `parallel`, `check` | Maximum duration of one agent session of the step, or of each command of a `check`. Past it, the run is blocked. |

| Step | Its own options |
|---|---|
| `talk` | `skills`, `writes`, `prompt` |
| `agent` | `agent` (required), `model`, `skills`, `prompt`, `writes` (a file of the run directory it may write), `output` (Zod schema of the result) |
| `parallel` | `agents` (names, or `{ agent, model, name, prompt, when, skills }`), `model`, `skills`, `prompt` |
| `check` | `commands` (defaults to the `checks` list of the run data) |
| `code` | `run` (your function; without it the step name must be a built-in) |

An option a step or a block does not have is refused when the workflow loads, such as `writes` on a `check`, `max` on an `each` or `commit` on a `loop`.

`model` is written `provider/model` or `provider/model#variant`, for example `"claude-agent/sonnet"`. It replaces the model of the agent's definition for that step, or for one agent of a `parallel` step. Without it, each agent keeps its own model.

`prompt` is a string or a function of `{ ticket, runDir, worktree, data, item, feedback }`.

`skills` lists skill ids. The plugin attaches them to the first prompt of the session, after the skills of the agent's definition, and checks in the message OpenCode stored that each one arrived with its content. A skill that is missing blocks the run, and the reason names it. The agent has nothing to load.

### Agents of a workflow

A workflow folder may carry its own agents, one file per agent in `agents/`. The file name is the agent's name. The plugin registers them in OpenCode. Give it a name no other agent has. When a built-in agent or an agent of your configuration has the same name, yours is the one that runs (OpenCode applies a configuration agent on top of the workflow's), the skills of the workflow's file are not attached, and `/workflow status` reports it.

```md
<!-- ~/.config/opencode/workflows/deliver/agents/planner-writer.md -->
---
description: Writes the implementation plan of a ticket
model: claude-agent/opus
skills: [writing-plans]
---
You write the plan of the ticket you are given, task by task.
```

Frontmatter: `description` (required), `model`, `mode` (`subagent` by default, `primary`, `all`), `hidden`, `skills`, `permissions` (list of `{ action, resource, effect }`). An unknown key is reported. The body is the agent's system prompt.

### From the earlier layout

Move `workflows/x.ts` to `workflows/x/x.ts`, and write `skill: "a"` as `skills: ["a"]`. A file left at the top of the workflows directory is not loaded; `/workflow status` lists it.

`onFail`, `max` and `then` on a step, and `each` on a step, were replaced by blocks. A workflow that still uses them is refused with the block to write; the table in [writing workflows](docs/writing-workflows.md#from-onfail-then-and-each) shows each rewrite. A run started by an older version cannot be resumed: `/workflow abort`, then start it again.

### Run data

The `data` an agent submits, and the object a `code` step returns, are merged into the run data. Later steps read it: `each("tasks", ...)` iterates `data.tasks`, `check` reads `data.checks`, `when: "sql"` runs a reviewer only if `data.sql` is truthy.

### Built-in code steps

| Name | What it does |
|---|---|
| `isolate` | Creates a branch and a git worktree for the run. Later steps work there. |
| `setup` | Runs the `setup` commands of the run data in the worktree. |
| `push` | Folds leftover changes into the last commit, checks signatures when signing is on, renames the branch to `data.branch` if set, pushes to `origin` and writes `pr.md` in the run directory. Needs `isolate` before it. |
| `cleanup` | Removes the worktree. The branch stays. |

## Piloting a run

Everything happens in the main session.

| Command | Effect |
|---|---|
| `/workflow status` | The workflow as a tree with the current step marked, the item and restart counters, the block reason, the run directory. |
| `/workflow approve`, `revise <remarks>`, `back [remarks]` | Answer a request for approval. |
| `/workflow pause` | Finish the current unit, then stop. |
| `/workflow resume` | Continue a paused, blocked or interrupted run. Finished steps are not replayed, and the restart counter of the loop the run was blocked in starts again from zero. |
| `/workflow abort` | Interrupt the agents and stop. The worktree and the state are kept. |
| `/workflow reload` | Reload the workflow folders and their agents. |

A blocked run tells you why and where to look. Fix the cause by hand, then `/workflow resume`. There is no way to force a step through.

While a run is running, talking or waiting for your approval, the main session cannot edit files (except the file a `talk` step names) nor commit. It is free again when the run is blocked, paused or over.

## What the plugin enforces

- **Order**: only the engine picks the next step.
- **Verdicts**: agents answer through the `workflow_submit` tool. A session that ends without calling it gets one reminder, then the run is blocked.
- **No commit by agents**: `git commit`, `git push` and `gh` are refused. After each agent, code checks that HEAD did not move. Reviewers must leave the work tree untouched.
- **Writes**: an agent can only edit inside the work directory, plus the one file of the run directory its step names with `writes`. Reviewers cannot edit at all. Step agents cannot launch subagents.
- **No permission prompt**: in a step's session, a permission that would be asked is denied.
- **State on disk**: each run has a directory with `state.json`, `events.ndjson` (every transition and every refused tool call), `reports/` and a final `report.md`.

Limits to know: the shell lock matches the command text, so a command that hides `git commit` behind a script is only caught by the HEAD check afterwards. Shell commands can still write files outside the work directory.

## Updates

Installed this way, the plugin follows the `main` branch, which only moves when a version is released.

OpenCode checks for a newer version when its server starts, but does not install it. The plugin does: when the terminal UI opens and a newer version exists, it asks OpenCode to install it, unless a run is at work, in which case it waits for the run to stop. It makes no network request of its own: the check and the install are OpenCode's. An install that fails is not tried again from the same version; you are told instead.

| You want | Do |
|---|---|
| To be told only | Set the option `autoUpdate` to `false`. When you choose, run `opencode plugin update` followed by the package string of your config; without it, every outdated plugin is updated |
| A fixed version | Install a release tag, for example `...opencode-steps.git#v0.1.0`. A release tag never moves, so nothing is installed after it |
| A version that can never change | Install a full commit hash: OpenCode never checks it |

# Getting started

## Install

Add the plugin to `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`:

```jsonc
{
  "plugins": ["opencode-steps@git+https://github.com/axelhamil/opencode-steps.git"]
}
```

Restart OpenCode, or run `opencode reload`. The plugin keeps itself up to date with the released versions; see [Updates](reference.md#updates) to pin a version or turn that off.

The plugin adds:

- the command `/workflow`, to pilot a run;
- one command per workflow folder found in `~/.config/opencode/workflows/`, and the agents those folders carry;
- the skill `writing-workflows`;
- in the terminal UI, the state of the run in the status line and in the sidebar.

## A first workflow

Create `~/.config/opencode/workflows/review-loop/review-loop.ts`. A workflow lives in a folder of its own name, next to the agents and prompt files it uses:

```ts
import type { Kit } from "opencode-steps/kit"

export default ({ workflow, agent, check, parallel, loop }: Kit) =>
  workflow("review-loop", [
    loop({ max: 2 }, [
      agent("write", { agent: "build", prompt: "Implement the ticket in the work directory, with its tests." }),
      check("checks", { commands: ["npm test"] }),
      parallel("review", {
        agents: [{ agent: "build", name: "correctness", prompt: "Review the uncommitted changes against the ticket." }],
      }),
    ]),
  ])
```

Then, in a session opened in a repository that has an `npm test` script:

```text
/workflow reload
/review-loop Add a multiply(a, b) function to math.js, with a test.
```

The session you typed this in is the main session of the run. Lines like these arrive in it as the run moves:

```text
[review-loop] write: succeeded -> checks
[review-loop] checks: succeeded -> review
[review-loop] review: succeeded -> DONE. Report: ~/.opencode/plan/<project>/<run>/report.md
```

If the tests fail, the `loop` restarts from `write` with their output as feedback, up to 2 times; the line reads `checks: failed -> loop restart 1/2 after "checks" failed -> write`. A finding of the reviewer restarts it the same way. If the cap is reached, or an agent returns nothing, the run is blocked and tells you why.

| `/workflow approve`, `/workflow revise <remarks>`, `/workflow back` | Your answer when a step asks for your approval |

# How it works

## One reducer decides

A run is a state: its status, its position in the tree of the workflow (a path of indexes from the top list down to the current step, plus one frame per enclosing block: the list of an `each` as read at its entry and the current item, the restarts used by a `loop`), the run data. An event changes it: a step succeeded, failed, or returned nothing; you approved, paused, resumed, aborted. One pure function, `reduce(workflow, state, event)`, gives the next state. Nothing else chooses a step, and no model is asked.

The engine runs the current step, turns what happened into an event, applies it, saves the state, and tells the main session. Then it runs the next step.

The next step is always the next one of the file, read top to bottom. Only the blocks change that: at the end of an `each` the run goes back to the first step of the block for the next item, and on a failure inside a `loop` it goes to the block's `repair`, then back to its first step. The progress lines say so: `-> tasks 3/5`, `-> loop restart 2/3 after "review" failed`.

When an `each` block has `commit`, the end of each pass is a place of its own in the tree, after the last step of the block: the engine commits there. If the commit fails, the run is blocked there, and `/workflow resume` tries the commit again before the next item.

## Three outcomes, not two

| What happened | Event | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| The step did its job | succeeded | Next step |
| The step verified and found a problem (`check`, `parallel` only) | failed | The closest enclosing `loop` runs its `repair` and restarts, up to `max` times. Outside any `loop`: blocked |
| Nothing usable came back: crash, timeout, usage limit, no verdict, an agent that says `blocked`, a lock that was broken | blocked | The run stops and waits for you |

Keeping the third apart is the point. A reviewer that crashed did not approve, and did not find a defect either.

## How an agent answers

Each step session has one way to end its work: the tool `workflow_submit`, with a status allowed for its step. The engine reads that verdict, never the agent's prose. A session that goes idle without calling it gets one reminder. Still nothing: blocked.

When a step declares an `output` schema, the submitted `data` is parsed against it. A mismatch is refused with the error, and the agent submits again.

## Skills are attached by code

A step that names `skills`, or whose agent file does, does not ask the agent to load them. The plugin attaches them to the first prompt of the session, and OpenCode puts each skill's content in that message. The plugin then reads the stored message back: every skill must be there with its content. One missing, or the prompt refused (an unknown skill id), and the session is interrupted and the run blocked with `skill "<id>" was not loaded`. Each proof is a `from: "skills"` line in `events.ndjson`, with the size of each skill. Later prompts, such as the reminder, carry no skills.

## Locks

Applied to every session of a step, twice: as permission rules when the session is created, and in a hook that runs before each tool call.

| Lock | Enforced by |
|---|---|
| No `git commit`, `git push`, `gh` | Hook on the command text, permission rules, then a check that HEAD did not move |
| Edits only inside the work directory, plus the file named by `writes` | Hook on the edit tools, with paths resolved |
| Reviewers do not edit | Permission rule, hook, then a comparison of the work tree before and after |
| No permission prompt | A permission that would be asked is denied |
| No subagent | Permission rule |

The main session is locked the same way while a run is running, talking or waiting for your approval. During a `talk` step it may write the one file named by `writes`. When the run is blocked or paused the main session is free again, so you can repair by hand.

Every refusal is written to `events.ndjson`.

What the locks do not cover: a shell command can still write a file anywhere, and a command that hides a commit behind a script is only caught afterwards by the HEAD check. The locks keep an honest agent on the path; they are not a sandbox.

## Why step sessions are not children

Step sessions are created at the top level, not as children of the main session. With a parent, OpenCode wakes the parent's model each time a child ends, and that model starts commenting and offering to act. Without one, the main session only receives the engine's progress lines. A step session is archived once its verdict is in; one that blocked stays visible so you can read it.

## Approval by command

OpenCode 2.3.0 gives a plugin no way to show a form in the terminal UI: forms only appear for a question asked by the model itself. So you answer with `/workflow approve`, `/workflow revise <remarks>` or `/workflow back`. A command cannot be auto-accepted, and it does not depend on a model deciding to ask.

## State on disk

The state is saved after every transition, by writing a temporary file and renaming it. If the save fails, the run stops and says so. After a crash or a restart, `/workflow resume` starts the interrupted unit again in a new session; finished steps are not replayed. The work tree is left as it was, so a unit that restarts may find partial work from its first attempt.

A state file that cannot be read is an error, never a fresh start. A run whose workflow file was edited so that the outline differs is blocked with `the workflow changed since the run started`: positions are indexes in the tree, so they would point at another step. The state carries a version: one written by an older version of the plugin is not driven, and `/workflow status` and `/workflow resume` say to abort it and start again. `/workflow abort` still works on it.

## What is not guaranteed

The engine proves that each step happened, in order, and returned an allowed verdict. It cannot prove that a review was good or that the tests test the right thing: `approved` is still a model's judgment, and a green check is worth what the repository's tests are worth. Keep reading the result.

# Reference

## Workflow folder

```
workflows/
  deliver/
    deliver.ts            the workflow file: <folder>/<folder>.ts, .js or .mjs
    agents/
      planner-writer.md   optional: agents of this workflow
    prompts/              anything else the workflow file reads itself
```

The workflow file's default export is a workflow, or a function that receives the kit and returns one. A folder without its workflow file, a workflow named differently from its folder, and a workflow file at the top of the workflows directory are reported by `/workflow status` and not loaded.

```ts
import type { Kit } from "opencode-steps/kit"

export default ({ workflow, talk, agent, parallel, check, code, each, loop, z }: Kit) => workflow("name", [/* steps and blocks */])
```

The workflow file runs on Bun: Bun's APIs (`import.meta.dir`, `Bun.file`, `Bun.$`) are available, and a top-level `await` runs at each load. For editor types, install `@types/bun` and set `"types": ["bun"]` in the workflows directory. The file is loaded again by `/workflow reload` when any file of its folder changed (folders named `node_modules` or starting with a dot excepted); a module it imports is not loaded again, so keep shared code in files it reads rather than imports.

The workflow name is the slash command and the folder name. It matches `[a-z][a-z0-9-]*`; `workflow` is reserved.

## Agent file

`<workflow>/agents/<name>.md`: a YAML frontmatter, then the agent's system prompt. `<name>` is the agent's name.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `description` | string, required | Shown in OpenCode's agent list |
| `model` | `provider/model` or `provider/model#variant` | Model of the agent |
| `mode` | `subagent`, `primary` or `all` | Defaults to `subagent` |
| `hidden` | boolean | Defaults to `false` |
| `skills` | list of skill ids | Skills attached to every step session of this agent, before the step's own |
| `permissions` | list of `{ action, resource, effect }` | `effect` is `allow`, `deny` or `ask`. Added after OpenCode's defaults |

An unknown field, a bad model or an unreadable file is reported and the agent is skipped. The same name in two workflows: the first in folder order is kept, the other is reported. Give it a name no other agent has. When a built-in agent or an agent of your configuration has the same name, yours is the one that runs (OpenCode applies a configuration agent on top of the workflow's), the skills of the workflow's file are not attached, and `/workflow status` reports it.

## Skills

`skills` on a step, on a `parallel` entry or on an agent file lists skill ids. The skills of a session are, without duplicates and in this order: those of the agent file, those of the step, those of the `parallel` entry. They are attached to the first prompt of the session (the prompt that starts a `talk` for the main session). The plugin then reads the message OpenCode stored: each skill must be there with its content. Otherwise the session is interrupted and the run is blocked with `skill "<id>" was not loaded`. Each proof is a line of `events.ndjson` with `from: "skills"` and the size of each skill.

## Steps

### `talk(name, options)`

The main session discusses with the user. It ends when the main session submits its verdict.

| Option | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `skills` | list of skill ids | Skills attached to the prompt that starts the discussion |
| `writes` | string | The only file it may write, relative to the run directory |
| `prompt` | string or function | Instructions for the discussion |

### `agent(name, options)`

One agent in its own session.

| Option | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `agent` | string, required | Name of the OpenCode agent |
| `model` | `provider/model` or `provider/model#variant` | Model for this step. Defaults to the model of the agent's definition |
| `skills` | list of skill ids | Skills attached to its first prompt, after those of its agent file |
| `prompt` | string or function | Instructions |
| `writes` | string | A file of the run directory it may write, besides the work directory |
| `output` | Zod schema | Shape of the `data` it must submit with `done`. The parsed fields join the run data |
| `deny` | list of `{ action, resource }` | Extra permission rules denied to its session |
| `timeoutMs` | number | Maximum duration of its session. Defaults to `agentTimeoutMinutes` |

Verdict statuses: `done`, `blocked`.

### `parallel(name, options)`

Several agents at the same time. They cannot edit, and must leave the work tree as they found it.

| Option | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `agents` | list, required | Agent names, or `{ agent, model, name, prompt, when, skills }`. `model` applies to that agent only; `name` labels the reports; `when` is a key of the run data that must be truthy for the agent to run; `skills` come after the step's |
| `model` | `provider/model` or `provider/model#variant` | Model for the agents that set none. Defaults to the model of each agent's definition |
| `skills` | list of skill ids | Skills attached to the first prompt of each agent |
| `prompt` | string or function | Instructions shared by the agents that have none of their own |
| `deny` | list of `{ action, resource }` | Extra permission rules denied to each session |
| `timeoutMs` | number | Maximum duration of each session. Defaults to `agentTimeoutMinutes` |

Verdict statuses: `approved`, `needs_fixes` (with at least one finding: `title`, `detail`, optional `file`), `blocked`. Any `needs_fixes` fails the step with the findings as the failure. Any `blocked` or missing verdict blocks the run.

### `check(name, options)`

| Option | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `commands` | list of strings | Commands run with `sh -c` in the work directory, in order. Defaults to the `checks` list of the run data. No command at all blocks the run |
| `timeoutMs` | number | Maximum duration of each command. Defaults to `checkTimeoutMinutes`. Past it, the run is blocked |

The first command that exits non-zero fails the step, with the last 60 lines of its output as the failure.

### `code(name, options)`

| Option | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `run` | function | Receives `{ ticket, runDir, worktree, directory, data, item }`. Returns `{ ok: true, value }` or `{ ok: false, error }`, or a promise of one |

Without `run`, the name must be a built-in; with `run`, the function replaces a built-in of the same name. A code step never fails: `{ ok: false, error }`, a thrown error or a failing built-in blocks the run.

| Built-in | Reads from the run data | Does | Adds to the run data |
|---|---|---|---|
| `isolate` | | Creates the branch `workflow/<run>` and a worktree in the run directory, from the current branch | `worktree`, `repo`, `base`, `branch` |
| `setup` | `setup` | Runs each command with `sh -c` in the work directory, 15 minutes at most each. A non-zero exit blocks the run | |
| `push` | `base`, `branch`, `title`, `tasks`, `checks` | Folds uncommitted changes into the last commit (or a `chore:` commit when none is ahead of `base`), refuses unsigned commits when `commit.gpgsign` is on, renames the branch to `data.branch`, pushes to `origin`, writes `pr.md`. Opens no pull request. Needs `isolate` before it and a commit ahead of `base` | `pushed`, `pullRequest` |
| `cleanup` | `repo` | Removes the worktree, without force. The branch stays | `worktree` |

## Blocks

### `each(key, options, steps)`

Runs `steps` top to bottom once per item of the list `data[key]`, in order. `options` can be left out: `each(key, steps)`.

| Option | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `commit` | string | Field of the item holding a commit subject. When a pass ends for an item whose field is a non-empty string and the work tree has changes, the work tree is committed with that subject. No `commit`, no commit |

- The list is read when the block is entered. An empty, missing or non-list value blocks the run; once the list exists, `/workflow resume` enters the block again.
- The list is kept as read at the entry of the block: a step that writes the same key during the passes changes the next entry of the block, not the items of this one.
- Every step of the block receives the current item: `item` in the prompt context and the code context, and an `Item` section in the prompt. Inside nested `each` blocks, `item` is the item of the closest block, and `items` holds the item of every enclosing block, outermost first; the prompt then gets them in a section of their own.
- Reports of `agent` steps inside the block are named `reports/<step>-<n>.md`, with one number per enclosing `each`, outermost first: `reports/<step>-2-1.md`.
- A commit that fails blocks the run; `/workflow resume` tries it again before the next item.

### `loop(options, steps)`

Runs `steps` top to bottom, and restarts them when one of them fails.

| Option | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `max` | integer, at least 1, required | Restarts allowed. The failure after the last restart blocks the run |
| `repair` | one `agent` step | Runs after a failure, with the failure as feedback, before the restart. Never runs when the block passes |

- Only `check` (a command exits non-zero) and `parallel` (a `needs_fixes`) fail. Every other problem blocks the run.
- A failure restarts the closest enclosing `loop`. Outside any `loop`, it blocks the run.
- Without `repair`, the failure is the feedback of the restarted steps, kept until a step that reads it (`talk`, `agent`, `parallel`) succeeds, and dropped when the run leaves the loop.
- A restart runs every step of the block again: an `each` inside starts again at its first item, items already done and committed included. To retry one item only, put the `loop` inside the `each`.
- The restart count starts again from zero each time the block is entered anew (next item of an enclosing `each`, restart of an enclosing `loop`) and on `/workflow resume` after a block inside it.

Blocks nest freely. Step names are unique in the whole tree, repair steps included.

An option a step or a block does not have is refused when the workflow loads: `writes` on a `check`, `max` on an `each`, `commit` on a `loop`, with the step kind or the block it belongs to.

| Option | Type | Meaning |

| `approve` | string | The run waits for the user after the step succeeds. The label is shown: `waiting for you to approve the <label>` |

`deny` is accepted by `agent` and `parallel` only, `timeoutMs` by `agent`, `parallel` and `check` only: anywhere else, it would do nothing, so the workflow is refused.

| Command | Effect |
|---|---|
| `/<workflow> <ticket>` | Starts a run. One unfinished run per session and per directory |
| `/workflow status` | The workflow as a tree, indented like the file: `✓` done, `↺` failed then repaired or restarted, `-` skipped, `▸` current (`✗` when blocked), `·` to come, with `each tasks (2/5)` and `loop (1/3 restarts)` on the blocks the run is in. A block takes the best mark of its steps. Then the block reason and the run directory. Without a run: the workflows loaded and the problems found in workflow folders and agent files |
| `/workflow approve` | Accepts the step that waits |

| `/workflow pause` | Stops after the current unit |
| `/workflow resume` | Continues a paused, blocked or interrupted run, from the session that types it. The restart counter of the loop the run was blocked in starts again from zero. A run started by an older version of the plugin is refused: abort it, then start it again |
| `/workflow abort` | Interrupts the agents and stops for good. The worktree and the state are kept |

## Updates

Installed this way, the plugin follows the `main` branch, which only moves when a version is released.

OpenCode checks for a newer version when its server starts, but does not install it. The plugin does: when the terminal UI opens and a newer version exists, it asks OpenCode to install it, unless a run is at work, in which case it waits for the run to stop. It makes no network request of its own: the check and the install are OpenCode's. An install that fails is not tried again from the same version; you are told instead.

| You want | Do |
|---|---|
| To be told only | Set the option `autoUpdate` to `false`. When you choose, run `opencode plugin update` followed by the package string of your config; without it, every outdated plugin is updated |
| A fixed version | Install a release tag, for example `...opencode-steps.git#v0.1.0`. A release tag never moves, so nothing is installed after it |
| A version that can never change | Install a full commit hash: OpenCode never checks it |

## Interface

In the terminal UI, the plugin adds a segment to the prompt's status line and a block to the sidebar. They show the run of the current session, or the unfinished run of its directory: workflow, current step, item and restart counters, the tree of steps, and what you can type when the run waits for you.

# Writing workflows

A workflow is a tree of steps. Each workflow has its own folder in the workflows directory: `deliver/deliver.ts` for the workflow `deliver`, plus `deliver/agents/` for its agents and any file its prompts read. An older `workflows/x.ts` moves to `workflows/x/x.ts`.

## How to read a workflow

```ts
workflow("deliver", [
  code("isolate"),
  agent("plan", { agent: "planner", output: Plan, approve: "plan" }),
  each("tasks", { commit: "commit" }, [
    loop({ max: 2 }, [
      agent("implement", { agent: "build" }),
      check("checks"),
    ]),
  ]),
  loop({ max: 3, repair: agent("fix", { agent: "build" }) }, [
    check("final-checks"),
    parallel("review", { agents: ["reviewer"] }),
  ]),
  code("push"),
])
```

- Read it top to bottom: that is the order in which steps run.
- `each` repeats its block once per item of a list, then the run goes on after it.
- `loop` restarts its block from its first step when a step of the block fails.
- `repair` runs once before that restart, with the failure to fix.
- `approve` makes the run wait for you after the step.

Nothing else moves the run, and no step names another step.

## Pick the step for each part

| The part is | Step |
|---|---|
| A discussion with you | `talk` |
| Work by one agent | `agent` |
| Several read-only opinions at once | `parallel` |
| Something a command can prove | `check` |
| Mechanical, no judgment needed | `code` |

Prefer `check` and `code` whenever a command can do the job: they cannot be talked out of it.

## Retry until it passes

Put the producer and what verifies it in a `loop`:

```ts
loop({ max: 2 }, [
  agent("write", { agent: "build" }),
  check("checks", { commands: ["npm test"] }),
]),
```

`checks` fails: the block restarts, `write` runs again with the failing output as `feedback`, then `checks` runs again. The failure stays with the restarted steps until a `talk`, `agent` or `parallel` step succeeds, and is dropped when the run leaves the loop. After 2 restarts, the third failure blocks the run: a loop always has an end. `max` is required.

Only `check` (a command exits non-zero) and `parallel` (a reviewer reports `needs_fixes`) fail. A failure outside any `loop` blocks the run, with a reason that says the step is not inside a `loop`.

## Repair with another agent

When the agent that repairs is not the one that produced, give the loop a `repair`:

```ts
loop({ max: 3, repair: agent("fix", { agent: "build" }) }, [
  check("checks", { commands: ["npm test"] }),
  parallel("review", { agents: ["reviewer"] }),
]),
code("push"),
```

When `review` passes, the run goes to `push` and `fix` never runs. When `checks` or `review` fails, `fix` runs with the failure, then `checks`, then `review` again.

## From onFail, then and each

These options were replaced by blocks. A workflow that still uses them is refused when it loads, with the block to write.

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| `agent("write", ...)`, `check("checks", { onFail: "write", max: 2 })` | `loop({ max: 2 }, [agent("write", ...), check("checks")])` |
| `parallel("review", { onFail: "fix", max: 3 })`, `agent("fix", { ..., then: "checks" })` | `loop({ max: 3, repair: agent("fix", ...) }, [check("checks"), parallel("review", ...)])` |
| `agent("implement", { ..., each: "tasks" })`, `check("checks", { onFail: "implement", max: 2 })` | `each("tasks", { commit: "commit" }, [loop({ max: 2 }, [agent("implement", ...), check("checks")])])` |

The commit of each item now happens only when the `each` block has `commit`.

## Ask for approval

```ts
agent("plan", { agent: "planner", approve: "plan" }),
```

After `plan` succeeds, the run waits and says `waiting for you to approve the plan`. You read the files of the run directory, then answer in the main session:

- `/workflow approve` continues;
- `/workflow revise <remarks>` runs the same step again with your remarks;
- `/workflow back [remarks]` returns to the closest `talk` step written before this one, inside blocks too.

## Talk steps

```ts
talk("scope", { skills: ["brainstorming"], writes: "spec.md", approve: "scope" }),
```

The main session receives the step's instructions and discusses with you. It can write one file, `spec.md` in the run directory, and nothing else. When you both agree, it submits its verdict and the run moves on (here, after your approval).

## One pass per item

An agent can return structured data. Declare its shape with `output`, a Zod schema from the kit:

```ts
import type { Kit } from "opencode-steps/kit"

export default ({ workflow, agent, check, code, each, loop, z }: Kit) => {
  const Plan = z.object({
    checks: z.array(z.string()).min(1),
    tasks: z.array(z.object({ title: z.string(), commit: z.string(), brief: z.string() })).min(1),
  })

  return workflow("deliver", [
    code("isolate"),
    agent("plan", { agent: "planner", output: Plan, approve: "plan" }),
    each("tasks", { commit: "commit" }, [
      loop({ max: 2 }, [
        agent("implement", { agent: "build" }),
        check("checks"),
      ]),
    ]),
    code("push"),
    code("cleanup"),
  ])
}
```

What happens:

1. `plan` submits `{ checks, tasks }`. A result that does not match the schema is refused, and the agent must submit again.
2. The fields join the run data. `each("tasks", ...)` runs its block once per task, in order, and every step of the block gets the task as `item`. `check` runs the commands of `data.checks`.
3. When the block passes for a task, code commits the work tree with the task's `commit` field as subject, then the next task starts. The loop inside starts each task with no restart used. The list is the one read when the block started: a step that writes `tasks` again does not change it.

A `loop` around an `each` restarts the whole list from its first task. Put the `loop` inside the `each` to retry one task.

Agents never commit. That is why each task ends up as exactly one commit. An empty or missing list blocks the run when the block is reached.

## Prompts

The engine writes most of the prompt for you: the rules about the verdict, the ticket, the current item, the feedback to address and the paths. Your `prompt` adds what is specific to the step.

```ts
agent("implement", {
  agent: "build",
  prompt: ({ data, item }) => `Follow the plan at ${data.planPath}. Do only this task: ${JSON.stringify(item)}. Write the test first.`,
})
```

## Skills

```ts
agent("implement", { agent: "build", skills: ["test-driven-development"] }),
```

`skills` are attached to the first prompt of the step's session by the plugin, not loaded by the agent. The plugin checks that each one arrived with its content; one missing blocks the run with `skill "test-driven-development" was not loaded`. `parallel` takes `skills` on the step and on each entry. An older `skill: "a"` is written `skills: ["a"]`.

## Agents of the workflow

An agent the workflow needs can live in its folder, `deliver/agents/planner-writer.md`, so the workflow carries everything it uses:

```md
---
description: Writes the implementation plan of a ticket
model: claude-agent/opus
skills: [writing-plans]
---
You write the plan of the ticket you are given, task by task.
```

Steps name it like any agent: `agent("plan", { agent: "planner-writer" })`. Its `skills` come before the step's. Other fields: `mode`, `hidden`, `permissions`. Give it a name no other agent has. When a built-in agent or an agent of your configuration has the same name, yours is the one that runs (OpenCode applies a configuration agent on top of the workflow's), the skills of the workflow's file are not attached, and `/workflow status` reports it.

## Types in your editor

A workflow file runs on Bun, the runtime OpenCode runs its plugins on, so Bun's APIs are available: `import.meta.dir`, `Bun.file`, `Bun.$`. It runs without any install. For types, inline documentation and no error in your editor, put these two files in the workflows directory and run `pnpm install` there:

```json
{
  "name": "workflows",
  "private": true,
  "type": "module",
  "devDependencies": {
    "@types/bun": "latest",
    "opencode-steps": "github:axelhamil/opencode-steps",
    "typescript": "latest"
  }
}
```

```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "ESNext",
    "module": "Preserve",
    "moduleResolution": "Bundler",
    "strict": true,
    "noEmit": true,
    "allowImportingTsExtensions": true,
    "skipLibCheck": true,
    "types": ["bun"]
  },
  "include": ["*/*.ts"]
}
```

Then start each workflow file with `import type { Kit } from "opencode-steps/kit"` and type the kit: `export default ({ workflow, agent }: Kit) => ...`. Hovering a step, an option or a built-in such as `code("isolate")` shows what it does, what it reads and writes in the run data, and examples.

Keep long prompts in files next to the workflow and read them when the file loads:

```ts
const brief = async (name: string): Promise<string> => Bun.file(`${import.meta.dir}/prompts/${name}.md`).text()
const plan = await brief("plan")
```

`/workflow reload` loads the workflow file again when any file of its folder changed, so an edited prompt is picked up. The `node_modules` folder and folders whose name starts with a dot are not read as workflows.

## Your own code step

```ts
code("changelog", {
  run: async ({ worktree, data }) => {
    const ok = await writeChangelog(worktree, data.tasks)

    return ok ? { ok: true, value: { changelog: true } } : { ok: false, error: "could not write the changelog" }
  },
})
```

Return `{ ok: true, value }` (an object merged into the run data, or `undefined`) or `{ ok: false, error }`, which blocks the run with that message.
